author: Gregory Thomas
title: Five people, including child, fell into Tomales Bay after a boat overturned. 'Heroic' fishermen sped to the rescue - NewsBreak
text:
By Gregory Thomas ,
11 hours ago A group of fishers had to be rescued after their boat capsized at the mouth of Tomales Bay on Saturday. (Sonoma County Sheriff's Office) Three heads were bobbing in the water.
A large wave had capsized a fishing boat near the mouth of Tomales Bay, dumping its occupants.
Rushing to a friend’s shrimp boat, father and son Willy and Cameron Vogler sped to the scene to look for survivors.
“We saw another big, head-high wave coming and we probably should have turned around, but once we saw people we went for it,” said Vogler, a lifelong local who runs the nearby private campground Lawson’s Landing.
Vogler’s boat was lifted into the air by the passing wave but landed gently, he said. Then he and his son approached the victims in the water and began hauling them aboard.
One was a 6-year-old child who, according to Vogler, had been trapped under the overturned vessel and was extracted by her father, who was extremely fatigued from the exertion of diving under the boat.
“That’s my worst nightmare,” Vogler said. “You have fishhooks and ropes and who knows what else hanging under there that you can get tangled up in.”
The Voglers, both fishermen, sped the three survivors back to Dillon Beach, where Marin County first responders awaited. Sonoma County authorities praised the Voglers’ quick work, calling them “heroic bystanders.”
The Saturday incident was first reported by a local news source, the West Marin Feed . A bystander had called 911 after seeing the boat overturn.
Two more passengers who had been aboard the vessel had swum to a remote, rocky pocket cove and were suffering from cold-water exposure, according to the Sonoma County Sheriff’s Office. The sheriff’s office deployed a helicopter with a rescuer dangling on a static rope attached to its skids. The rescuer was lowered to the beach and the helicopter extracted the survivors, one at a time, depositing them on a nearby bluff.
All five victims were transported to a local hospital.
“We commend the outstanding teamwork among all responding agencies and the courageous bystanders whose quick actions helped save lives that day,” the sheriff’s office wrote in a Facebook post .
The boat, a 20-foot-long fishing vessel, is still adrift.
Vogler wants to warn other boaters and fishers who might be planning to run in and out of Tomales Bay for dungeness crab season. The shallow sandbar where the vessel capsized, located about a mile south of Tomales Point at the bay’s mouth, is notoriously dangerous this time of year due to the potential for large, erratic waves.
“Every couple of years someone gets killed on that bar going out for crab,” Vogler said. “If they’re not sure if the bar is safe, then they shouldn’t go out there.”
